title: Cycle 23: Server-side local-auth TTL + client hardening
weak_spots: Cycle 22 proactive refresh used a client-only 5-minute heuristic with no server visibility into actual token lifetime
A server-side token rotation left TriOS holding an expired token until the next 403 forced a reactive refresh
No distinct status code distinguished 'token missing/invalid' from 'token expired', complicating retry policies
Queen dashboard showed token state but not the server-issued TTL or precise countdown
Middleware validation only knew the current token value, not whether the token had reached its expiry boundary
competitors: SwiftAI Boilerplate AsyncStream AuthState + proactive 60s-before-expiry refresh
TokenEater AppErrorState enum + menu-bar recovery banner + silent keychain reads
omi AuthSessionCoordinator single-flight refresh + definitive death classifier
Ory token lifecycle management + refresh-token rotation + family invalidation
onelake-explorer-macos Sign In Again menu-bar action
Hono auth patterns: access tokens ~15 min, refresh tokens ~7 days, /auth/refresh rotation

variants.name: Keep client-only heuristic refresh
variants.summary: Refresh every 5 minutes regardless of server TTL. Simple but causes unnecessary fetch load and still allows expired-token windows.

variants.name: Server-side TTL metadata + precise client refresh
variants.summary: BrowserOS LocalAuthService issues tokens with issuedAt, expiresAt, expiresInSeconds, ttlSeconds; /auth/local-token returns full metadata; middleware rejects expired tokens with 401; TriOS LocalAuthProvider parses TTL and refreshes 60 seconds before expiry; Queen dashboard shows TTL metadata.

variants.name: Refresh-token rotation + family invalidation
variants.summary: Issue a short-lived access token and a longer-lived refresh token; /auth/refresh rotates both and tracks token families. Strongest revocation story but requires session storage and rotation logic.

lessons: Server-side TTL metadata eliminates guesswork: the client should refresh based on the issuer's expiry, not a local heuristic.
A distinct 401 for expired tokens lets middleware and client telemetry classify failures precisely without leaking the secret.
Parsing ISO8601 with a fixed TimeZone(secondsFromGMT: 0) on the client avoids timezone drift against server timestamps.
Actor-isolated LocalAuthProvider + single-flight refreshTask naturally deduplicates forced refreshes triggered by concurrent 403 retries.
Monitor metadata should stay token-free; include issuedAt/expiresAt/ttlSeconds for dashboards, never the token value.
